source.title: A Probabilistic Method to Predict Classifier Accuracy on Larger Datasets given Small Pilot Data
source.authors: Ethan Harvey; Wan-Su Chen; D. Kent; Michael C. Hughes

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates power-law and arctan learning-curve extrapolators on medical-image classifier accuracy as training-set size increases. This is a different modality, metric, and setup from language-model pretraining-loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study’s results concern medical-image classifier AUROC as a function of training-set size, not language-model pretraining loss, parameter-count scaling, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Results about power-law predictors and image-task extrapolation are recorded under V5. Related-work statements about other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds a Gaussian-process extrapolator for medical-image classifier AUROC against training-set size. Its classifier is a linear head on a frozen ImageNet ViT. A saturating power law, (1-ε)−θ1·x^θ2, serves as one of two GP mean functions. Every recorded row is the quantized likelihood of the authors' own extrapolator (GP pow or GP arc) against a uniform baseline. That measures how well calibrated their method's predictive density is, not whether loss or error follows a power law. It does not test the power-law form in a new regime (V5) or large-run extrapolation (V2). Nothing touches language models, pretraining loss, compute or model size. The power-law-versus-arctan comparison of curve forms is recorded under fits_no_version instead.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that their GP extrapolator (APEx-GP) matches deterministic curve fits in pointwise error while adding uncertainty estimates. They recommend the power-law mean for its long-range error, quantized likelihood and coverage. They concede it is not universally preferred: on effusion its error was worse than the deterministic power law. They say further work is needed beyond their modalities, train-set sizes, architectures and the AUROC metric. Their coverage is often 100% against a 95% target, so the intervals are too wide.
record.recipe_differences: Probabilistic Gaussian-process extrapolation of medical-image classifier AUROC against training-set size; it compares power-law and arctan means and is not a language-model pretraining-loss scaling-law experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Curve mean (power law versus arctan), extrapolation range, and task/label affect reported results.

fits_no_version.finding: For linear-probe AUROC versus training-set size on medical images, a saturating power-law mean extrapolates better long-range (2–50x) than an arctan mean. GP arc is much worse on Infiltration (1.1% vs 25.2% quantized likelihood), PLAX (39.0% vs 64.8%) and A4C (24.5% vs 58.2%). Arctan wins on Viral (24.6% vs 12.3%). Long-range RMSE of the deterministic power law is 0.40–3.97 AUROC points, against up to 15.35 for arctan (Table D.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A saturating power law in training-set size extrapolates downstream classifier AUROC of transfer-learned image models over 2–50x more data better than arctan curve forms.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 225, Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2023
record.problems: The evidence is confined to medical-image classifier tasks, AUROC, the stated ViT-based classifier procedure, and the tested training-set sizes. The authors note it is not universally preferred and say further work is needed beyond their modalities, sizes, architectures, and metric. Reported coverage is often wider than the 95% target.
record.rows_left_out: The study also reports RMSE tables and coverage results (Tables 3, D.1, D.2, G.1, and H.1). These additional separately reported outcomes are omitted to keep the record within the 60-row limit after retaining every short- and long-range quantized-likelihood comparison in Table 2.

untested.parts: All of it: no language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
All of it: no language-model loss extrapolation. Data-size extrapolation of linear-probe AUROC (2–50x) is outside the version.
No test of whether a power law describes loss or error in a new regime. Only the calibration of a GP extrapolator using a saturating power-law mean is reported, on 360–20k samples.
All of it for language-model laws.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool or method paper (T4). The power law is a component of the authors' extrapolator, and the rows score that extrapolator's calibration. Two rows carry wrong values: r37 should be 38.2 and r39 should be 12.3 (Table 2). With these corrected, the authors' 'power law wins clearly in 5 of 6' holds with Viral as the arctan win. Table 2 long-range has 9 tasks, not 6. The record's supports and limits_scope labels for V5 should be dropped. The study cites Kaplan et al. only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Predicting language-model loss for runs orders of magnitude larger from smaller runs.
Effects of language-model architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The paper tests image-classifier accuracy versus training-set size on medical image tasks; it does not test video, language models, repeated-data regimes, or transfer/fine-tuning regimes beyond its stated classifier procedure.
Downstream-task predictability from language-model scale or pretraining loss.
How fitting choices affect language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation, and whether language-model curves bend away from a power law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Power-law-mean GP extrapolations on the tested medical-image classifier tasks, especially long-range cases
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that the power-law mean wins clearly in 5 of 6 long-range cases and essentially ties in another; its reported quantized likelihoods are above the uniform baseline in most listed tasks (r31, r35, r37, r39, r41, r43, r45, r47). This supports only image-classifier accuracy-versus-training-set-size extrapolation.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tasks where curve-form performance differs or power-law prediction is comparatively weak
reader_labels.reason: The arctan result is much higher for short-range TMED-2 A2C; the long-range power-law result is weak for effusion and A2C, and the arctan infiltration result is below the uniform baseline (r23, r24, r33, r35, r36, r47, r48).
